name: Perp-spot basis calm (leverage not frothy) + RSI dip — buy dips only when perps are calm (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why a calm basis leads better dip outcomes): the perp-spot basis is the revealed price of leverage. A HIGH positive basis (rich premium) means perps are crowded-long and over-leveraged — dips there cascade as longs get liquidated. A CALM basis (below a modest-premium ceiling) means leverage is not overheated, so a dip is orderly spot-driven weakness that recovers rather than a liquidation spiral. The basis conditions the leverage environment ahead of the dip's resolution, so it tells a safe dip from a dangerous one. We use the basis as a CALM-LEVERAGE FILTER (perp_spot_basis below a ceiling) on an RSI dip-buy, exiting if the basis spikes up into froth. This is a distinct ROLE for the basis vs the discount-contrarian/continuation specs (there it is the trigger; here it is a leverage safety filter). DISCONFIRMER 1: if a plain RSI-dip buy matches the deflated Sharpe, the basis filter adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2: if the fitted ceiling is so high it never excludes frothy bars, the filter is inert. tier0 derivative read; low-confidence until validated OOS.
catalyst: perp_spot_basis is BELOW a fitted modest-premium ceiling (leverage not overheated) while RSI has dipped.
